display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma on SM103.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma on SM103.

On SM103 (`sm_103a`, GB300), dense 4-bit block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` (`mxf4` and `mxf4nvf4`) supports `K=96` (48 bytes per MMA step) in addition to `K=64` (32 bytes per MMA step), reducing the number of MMA instructions per K tile by up to 1.5× and lifting 2-CTA throughput from ~9.73 PFLOP/s to up to 14.62 PFLOP/s on 256×256×768 tiles.

`tcgen05.mma` now uses `K=96` steps on `sm_103a` for dense 4-bit block-scaled MMAs with SMEM operands and 128B swizzle, when `M=128` and `b_scale` is padded along `N` to exactly 128 or 256 rows. All other configurations are unchanged.

display_title: Fix NaN Hessian from jacfwd(jacfwd(...)) for locally constant clipped SVD

head_commit.message:
Fix NaN Hessian from jacfwd(jacfwd(...)) for locally constant clipped SVD

In _svd_jvp_rule the reciprocal guard for the singular-value
differences only covered the diagonal (via an identity matrix), so
degenerate off-diagonal pairs (e.g. all-zero singular values) left a
0 denominator, producing inf which became NaN (inf * 0) under a
second forward-mode pass. Guard every entry where s_diffs is zero
instead, so F is 0 there. Reverse-mode paths already masked the NaN
through the clamp select, which is why only fwd/fwd was affected.

Add a regression test checking all four jacfwd/jacrev Hessian
combinations on the clamped SVD sum from #42682.

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42682

display_title: Allow `device_put` to a memory space in eager `shard_map`

head_commit.message:
Allow `device_put` to a memory space in eager `shard_map`

The eager `shard_map` rule for `device_put_p` raised a `ValueError` for
any non-`None` destination. However, besides devices and shardings, the
destination can be a `jax.memory.Space`, for example the host offload in
`jax.checkpoint` with
`save_and_offload_only_these_names(..., offload_dst="pinned_host")`.
Under `jit` these are supported, so the same code failed only in eager
mode.

Moving between host and device memory keeps each shard on its own
device, so let the rule run `device_put_p` when the destination is a
`jax.memory.Space`. Explicit devices and shardings still raise, and all
destinations are checked before any move runs.

head_commit.message:
Fix warm-cache jit silently misreading non-native byte order

With a warm cache, jitted functions silently misread arrays with
non-native byte order: PyArgSignatureOfValue converted the NumPy dtype
to an XLA primitive type, losing byte order, so native and swapped
arrays shared a JIT cache signature and the swapped bytes were read as
native values. Cold calls were correctly rejected by Python
abstractification (dtypes.check_valid_dtype).

Return InvalidArgument for swapped arrays so the C++ pjit path falls
back to Python (fallback_to_cache_miss), which raises the same
TypeError as the cold path.

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42712.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.execution_options for per-call IFRT execute options

Expose ifrt::ExecuteOptions::custom_options from JAX via a
jax.execution_options(custom_options=...) context manager. Options set
inside the context are forwarded to every execution dispatched from the
current thread, for both jitted and AOT-compiled functions, through the
C++ fast path and the Python fallback.

The options are stored in a regular jax config (thread-local with a
global fallback) as a plain dict and converted to an AttributeMap in C++
on dispatch. They are not part of the jit cache key, so changing them
never retraces or recompiles. Nested contexts merge, inner values win.
Supported value types are bool, int, float, str and sequences of int.

Bump jaxlib_extension_version to 526.

head_commit.message:
Mark complex exp, sinh, and cosh infinite border regions as inaccurate in lax_test.

https://github.com/openxla/stablehlo/pull/3039 updates StableHLO's
complex math expander lowering of `stablehlo.exponential` to follow C99
Annex G.6.3.1 when the real part is infinite and the imaginary part is
non-finite: `exp(-inf + I*y)` returns `0` and `exp(+inf + I*y)` returns
`+inf + nanj`. Because complex `sinh` and `cosh` lower through
`stablehlo.exponential`, `sinh(±inf ± infj)` evaluates to `±inf + nanj`
and `cosh(±inf ± infj)` evaluates to `+inf + nanj`.

Meanwhile, `mpmath` still evaluates all three operations at
`(±inf ± infj)` to `nan + nanj`, causing `testSuccessOnComplexPlane` for
`exp`, `sinh`, and `cosh` (`complex64` and `complex128`) in
`FunctionAccuracyTest` to fail on CPU and GPU.

Mark `'ninf'`, `'pinf'`, `'ninfj'`, and `'pinfj'` as known inaccurate
regions for `exp` and `cosh`, and expand `'ninf.imag'` and `'pinf.imag'`
to `'ninf'` and `'pinf'` for `sinh` on CPU and CUDA (`'ninfj.real'` and
`'pinfj.real'` are already listed for `sinh`). This remains
backward-compatible with older XLA/StableHLO builds because
`testFailureOnComplexPlane` skips regions that still match `mpmath`.

head_commit.message:
[jax] Fix csr_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

When `nse` exceeds the number of nonzeros, `_csr_fromdense_impl` masks the padded `data` entries to zero and records only the true nonzeros in `indptr` (`indptr[-1] == nnz`). `_csr_fromdense_jvp` did not apply the same mask: for padded positions `>= indptr[-1]`, `_csr_to_coo` produces `row = M.shape[0]`, which `_csr_extract` clamps to the last row `M.shape[0] - 1` of `Mdot` instead of returning zero. Because `CSC.fromdense` delegates to `csr_fromdense` on the transposed matrix, `CSC.fromdense` has the same bug. This produces nonzero forward-mode tangents and wrong forward-mode higher derivatives when `nse > nnz`.

Mask `data_dot` in `_csr_fromdense_jvp` with the same `true_nonzeros` mask used in `_csr_fromdense_impl`, matching the `_coo_fromdense_jvp` fix for https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40624. Primal outputs are unchanged.

When `nse` exceeds the number of nonzeros, `_csr_fromdense_impl` masks the padded `data` entries to zero and records only the true nonzeros in `indptr` (`indptr[-1] == nnz`). `_csr_fromdense_jvp` did not apply the same mask: for padded positions `>= indptr[-1]`, `_csr_to_coo` produces `row = M.shape[0]`, which `_csr_extract` clamps to the last row `M.shape[0] - 1` of `Mdot` instead of returning zero. Because `CSC.fromdense` delegates to `csr_fromdense` on the transposed matrix, `CSC.fromdense` has the same bug. This produces nonzero forward-mode tangents and wrong forward-mode higher derivatives when `nse > nnz`.

Mask `data_dot` in `_csr_fromdense_jvp` with the same `true_nonzeros` mask used in `_csr_fromdense_impl`, matching the `_coo_fromdense_jvp` fix for https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40624. Primal outputs are unchanged.

head_commit.message:
Make HiPrim hash and eq include in_aval_flat, in_tree, out_avals_flat, out_tree.

Unlike `core.Primitive`, every `HiPrim` call creates a new object that saves its input and output types on `self`.

`HiPrim.__eq__` and `HiPrim.__hash__` previously checked only the class, `params`, and `effects`, ignoring those saved types.

For example, suppose an eager `shard_map` calls `hijax.nonzero(x, size=5, axes=(1,))` on `int32[2, 8]` and then on `int32[2, 0]`:

1. Call 1 builds `prim_1` (expecting `int32[2, 8]`) and caches a `jit` wrapper keyed on `prim_1`.
2. Call 2 builds `prim_2` (expecting `int32[2, 0]`), but `prim_2 == prim_1` is `True` because both have `size=5` and `axes=(1,)`.
3. The cache returns Call 1's `jit` wrapper (still holding `prim_1`), which raises a type mismatch when given `int32[2, 0]`.

Include the flattened input and output types and their PyTree structures in `HiPrim.__eq__` and `HiPrim.__hash__`. Use the flattened fields rather than raw `in_avals` and `out_aval` because those attributes can hold unhashable lists or dicts.

communicate. Exported programs keep the layouts until 2026-12-01.

display_title: [oneAPI] Fix symbolic SVD transpose handling

head_commit.message:
[oneAPI] Fix symbolic SVD transpose handling

When constraints establish m <= n, the comparison m < n can
remain inconclusive because equality is allowed. Fall back to
m <= n in the shared CUDA, ROCm, and OneAPI gesvd lowering.
Continue raising if the fallback comparison is also inconclusive.

Add one small float32 regression case with symbolic dimensions
and no size bounds, making CUDA/ROCm export select gesvd.
